description: Maharashtra has launched CM-SRISTHI, a five-year scheme to boost research and innovation in higher education, Minister Chandrakant Patil said. Running from 2026-27 to 2030-31, it will focus on AI, quantum computing, semiconductors and robotics. Public universities will establish Schools of Technology, while new Centres of Excellence will be created at major institutions across the state.
body_lead: Mumbai: In a major push to transform Maharashtra into a global hub for research, innovation, and futuristic technologies, the State Department of Higher and Technical Education has announced the launch of the ‘CM-SRISTHI’ scheme (Scheme for Research, Innovations and Technological Hubs in Higher Education Institutions). The announcement was made by Higher and Technical Education Minister Chandrakant Patil following the issuance of the Government Resolution passed in the recent cabinet meeting.
